C01.signature: Workers stage and tally order-specific components before insertion; accurate order lists and sufficient bench space enable fewer selection errors and shorter selection/checking time.
C01.reason: All six share checked staging, with preparation included. Stage timing evaluates this intervention; it does not make D2-F05 an additional mechanism match.

C02.signature: Customers receive an ordered-layout diagram locating the short partition; equivalent verified parts distinguish placement ambiguity from physical insertion difficulty.
C02.reason: Preserves the agreed guidance/diagnostic family. Every member tests placement with equivalent contents; tighter controls do not add a mechanism.

C03.signature: Workers spatially check order-specific parts and supply corresponding destinations for customer placement; accurate, distinguishable mappings connect completeness and guidance. Carriers and mat/slip variants assume correspondence remains interpretable after packing.
C03.reason: Each member supplies both linked representations and compatible omission/placement predictions. Their shared primary relation is coherent; linkage beyond independently accurate checking plus guidance remains unresolved. D2-F04 matches only secondary customer-assembly branches in P001/P002/P003/P006/P008 A1, not every member. P001 closure enforcement is a separate speculative relation; automatic encoding in P005 is unspecified. Neither upgrades this primary family.

C04.signature: Workers independently derive an accepted-order check, validate the shared mapping and catch internally consistent wrong map/kit pairs; authority and independence of the source are required.
C04.reason: Preserves the agreed five-member family: each specifies the same common-source-error challenge and independent correction path. New is local to the incomplete archive, not demonstrated efficacy.

C05.signature: Workers cross-swap compatible partitions and slots, controlling wear/order; difficulty following a part, slot or pairing discriminates their contributions.
C05.reason: Unchanged singleton anchor: crossed attribution adds a specific discriminator to the archive question.

C06.signature: Compatibility screening retains difficult insertions in the workshop and transfers candidate easy ones through mapped kits; compare customer retries and total screening/carrier overhead.
C06.reason: Unchanged singleton anchor: diagnostic results control allocation. Prediction depends on screening generalizing to customers; null Distill remains an execution failure.

C07.signature: Workers change short-partition insertion sequence with identical parts; obstruction by earlier partitions predicts sequence-dependent retries, controlling learning and loosening.
C07.reason: Unchanged singleton anchor: procedural obstruction is a distinct proposed discriminator.

C08.signature: Insertion resistance deflects a compliant guide and exposes a visible pre-seating cue; witness-only versus guide-plus-witness tests feedback, retries and damage under safe elastic travel.
C08.reason: Unchanged singleton anchor. Preserve the agreed lost retention: Distill names the guide/witness but omits resistance causing deflection and the cue.

C09.signature: Workers compare blocked and interleaved identical workloads; switching predicts extra selection/checking time independent of layout complexity, assuming representative reusable samples.
C09.reason: Preserves the agreed two-member family: both manipulate sequence and measure stage time. Matching improves attribution without a new mechanism.
